questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: language, weather, university, bigger city, high standard of living, possibility to surf

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I count my exchange semester as one of the best experiences in my life. You get the opportunity to meet a lot of new people from all over the world, who mostly share the same intention: everyone is new to the city, in need to make friends and make the best out of those few months. You learn a lot about different cultures, you experience the study life in a different country, different ways of teaching, partying, hanging out and you'll have the opportunity to travel around and get to know the country better.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I got all information via email. The exchange office is very unreliable, they do not reply to emails and calls and their office was under construction, so there was no possibility to talk to them in person.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They offer a shuttle bus service from the airport to UNSW but I didn't use it because they never got back to me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy for me. I used the app flatmates and found a place with two housemates from Sydney. In Sydney it is very common that people who don't know each other before, live together in a shared house. I recommend to arrive in Sydney a few weeks earlier before everyone else does to avoid ending up with an overpriced, shitty place. You will also have to go to room inspections in person to have a chance.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Sydney is huge and the public transportation system is not that good. The main campus of UNSW is in Kensington which is a bit off from the city center. However, it is close to Coogee Beach and Maroubra Beach and a lot of students live there. I had to take the bus to uni (45 min one way). Biking is almost impossible, no bike lanes, a lot of cars & Sydney is very hilly...

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The deadline of changing the courses ends before the classes start, so there's no possibility to change if you end up not liking the course.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You will get an email with a registration link. Then you can choose the courses you want and they have to get approved by the authorities first. Then they will enroll you manually.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not really any help at all. The exchange office is very unreliable, they do not reply to emails and calls and their office was under construction, so there was no possibility to talk to them in person.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: UNSW does it manually for the exchange students and they were very slow with replying or didn't reply at all. I only managed to get enrolled in the courses I want one week before the classes started and only because I went there in person and begged them to help me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I recommend to go to the nucleus student hub at the main library of UNSW, they will then try to get in touch with the exchange office.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It really depends on the courses. The actuarial courses at UNSW are known to be quite hard compared to other subjects. I struggled with one course and most in my class did so as well, but at the end they gave everyone good marks.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: we had to do quizzes online every week which ended up being very time consuming

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are over 300 clubs of all kinds. Everyone will find something they like.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The outdoor club and the surf club are the two biggest clubs. They organize trips, get-togethers, social events...

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as you can. Road trips along the coast, discover Sydney...

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, people are very relaxed, open and friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Enroll in a course with only a few students. Go to the Roundhouse after class, it's the student bar at campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: openness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join one of the clubs from UNSW, great way to meet new people. 
Go to the introduction week to get freebies. 
Go to the foodhub to get free food. (Every Monday, Wednesday, Friday).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses might take a lot of your time. I would recommend to choose easy courses to have more free time to do other stuff.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new friends from all over the world that I met during my exchange.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Money. I got a student job at a cafe, which was quite easy. You are allowed to work with the student visa.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
